SELECT l.lead_id, l.business_id, l.trace_id, l.from_email, l.subject, l.body,
       l.raw_payload->>'from_name' AS from_name,
       b.name AS business_name, b.industry
FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads l
JOIN vaibhavcapstone_businesses b USING (business_id)
WHERE l.lead_id = $1 AND l.status IN ('RECEIVED');

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ systemInstruction: { parts: [{ text: "You classify and extract structured data from one inbound email received by a business.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose, exactly these keys:
{"classification":"ENQUIRY|NOT_ENQUIRY|SPAM","contact_name":string|null,"contact_email":string|null,"company":string|null,"budget_value":number|null,"budget_currency":string|null,"product_interest":string[],"urgency":"high"|"medium"|"low"|null,"location":string|null (customer city/region relevant for delivery or visit; NOT rooms, sites or descriptions like a terrace),"confidence":number}
Rules:
- ENQUIRY = a potential customer asking about buying the business's products/services.
- NOT_ENQUIRY = legitimate mail that is not a purchase enquiry (vendor pitches, partnerships, invoices, job applications).
- SPAM = scams, phishing, lotteries, unsolicited mass mail.
- Extract ONLY facts explicitly present in the email or its headers. Use null when absent. NEVER guess or invent values.
- contact_name: a name written in the body/signature; otherwise the From-Name header if it looks like a real personal name (e.g. first + last name). A bare handle, nickname, or single lowercase word is NOT a name -> null.
- budget_value: total numeric budget in the currency mentioned. Convert Indian notation (1 lakh = 100000, 1 crore = 10000000).
- product_interest: short lowercase category words for what they want (e.g. "desks", "office-chairs", "sofas", "beds", "dining", "bookshelves", "outdoor").
- urgency reflects TIME pressure only: high = explicit deadline or delivery window within ~a month (e.g. "within 2-3 weeks", "by end of August") or urgent wording; medium = implied near-term need or an event/move without an exact date; low = no time signal at all (price/availability questions alone are low).
- confidence: 0-1, how confident you are in classification AND extraction combined, given how clear and complete the email is.
  Calibration: 0.9+ = clear, well-formed, specific email; ~0.7 = clear intent but sparse details; BELOW 0.5 = garbled, txt-speak, or too vague to extract anything meaningful (e.g. "hey u sell stuf?? price??").
If the message is garbled or barely intelligible: set EVERY extraction field to null, product_interest to [], and confidence below 0.5. Do not extract urgency or interests from garbled fragments." }] }, contents: [{ role: 'user', parts: [{ text: ('Business receiving the email: ' + $('Fetch Lead').first().json.business_name + ' (industry: ' + ($('Fetch Lead').first().json.industry || 'unknown') + ')

Email:
From: ' + ($('Fetch Lead').first().json.from_email || 'unknown') + '
From-Name: ' + ($('Fetch Lead').first().json.from_name || '(none)') + '
Subject: ' + ($('Fetch Lead').first().json.subject || '(none)') + '

' + ($('Fetch Lead').first().json.body || '')) }] }], generationConfig: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' } }) }}

parameters.query:
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::text AS lead, $2::text AS biz, $3::text AS trc, $4::jsonb AS r),
cfg AS (SELECT COALESCE((b.config->>'min_confidence')::numeric, 0.6) AS mc
        FROM vaibhavcapstone_businesses b, p WHERE b.business_id = p.biz),
ns AS (SELECT CASE
  WHEN (SELECT r->>'classification' FROM p) = 'SPAM' THEN 'DISCARDED_SPAM'
  WHEN (SELECT r->>'classification' FROM p) = 'NOT_ENQUIRY' THEN 'DISCARDED_NOT_ENQUIRY'
  WHEN COALESCE((SELECT (r->>'confidence')::numeric FROM p), 0) < (SELECT mc FROM cfg) THEN 'NEEDS_REVIEW'
  ELSE 'EXTRACTED' END AS st),
ext AS (INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_extractions
  (lead_id, business_id, classification, contact_name, contact_email, company,
   budget_value, budget_currency, product_interest, urgency, location, raw_llm_output)
  SELECT p.lead, p.biz, p.r->>'classification', p.r->>'contact_name', p.r->>'contact_email', p.r->>'company',
         NULLIF(p.r->>'budget_value','')::numeric, p.r->>'budget_currency',
         COALESCE(p.r->'product_interest','[]'::jsonb), p.r->>'urgency', p.r->>'location', p.r
  FROM p
  ON CONFLICT (lead_id) DO UPDATE SET classification=EXCLUDED.classification, contact_name=EXCLUDED.contact_name,
    contact_email=EXCLUDED.contact_email, company=EXCLUDED.company, budget_value=EXCLUDED.budget_value,
    budget_currency=EXCLUDED.budget_currency, product_interest=EXCLUDED.product_interest,
    urgency=EXCLUDED.urgency, location=EXCLUDED.location, raw_llm_output=EXCLUDED.raw_llm_output
  RETURNING lead_id),
upd AS (UPDATE vaibhavcapstone_leads
  SET status = (SELECT st FROM ns),
      status_detail = CASE WHEN (SELECT st FROM ns) = 'NEEDS_REVIEW'
        THEN jsonb_build_object('reason','low_confidence','confidence',(SELECT r->>'confidence' FROM p),'resume_from','classify')
        ELSE status_detail END,
      updated_at = now()
  WHERE lead_id = (SELECT lead FROM p) AND status IN ('RECEIVED','NEEDS_REVIEW')
  RETURNING status),
ev AS (INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_events (business_id, lead_id, trace_id, agent, action, actor, detail)
  SELECT p.biz, p.lead, p.trc, 'classify-extract', 'LEAD_CLASSIFIED', 'system',
         jsonb_build_object('classification', p.r->>'classification', 'confidence', p.r->>'confidence',
                            'new_status', (SELECT st FROM ns), 'attempt', $5::int)
  FROM p RETURNING event_id)
SELECT (SELECT st FROM ns) AS new_status, (SELECT lead FROM p) AS lead_id,
       (SELECT r->>'classification' FROM p) AS classification;

nodes.name: Persist Classification+Extraction
nodes.notes: One atomic CTE: upsert extraction, route lead status (SPAM/NOT_ENQUIRY discard, low confidence -> NEEDS_REVIEW, else EXTRACTED), log event. Confidence threshold from business config (default 0.6).

parameters.query:
WITH upd AS (UPDATE vaibhavcapstone_leads
  SET status='NEEDS_REVIEW',
      status_detail = jsonb_build_object('reason','llm_output_invalid','errors',$4,'resume_from','classify'),
      updated_at=now()
  WHERE lead_id=$1 AND status IN ('RECEIVED') RETURNING lead_id)
INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_events (business_id, lead_id, trace_id, agent, action, actor, detail)
VALUES ($2, $1, $3, 'classify-extract', 'LLM_OUTPUT_INVALID', 'system', jsonb_build_object('errors', $4))
RETURNING event_id;

parameters.content:
## Reading the email

An enquiry has arrived and been written down. Now we need two things from it: **is this a real customer enquiry**, and **what facts are in it** — who wrote it, which company, what they want, how much they can spend, how soon.

That's the whole job here: turn a paragraph of English into tidy, checkable facts. Read left to right — get ready → ask the AI → if the answer came back unusable, ask once more → save what we got, or hand it to a person.

### Getting ready

**Someone hands us a job.** This step never runs on its own. The workflow before it calls it and passes a small job ticket carrying the business, the enquiry and a tracking number.

**Check the ticket is complete.** If any required detail is missing we stop right here with a clear error, rather than carry on with half a job. The error workflow catches it, writes it down and emails the operator.

**Fetch the enquiry.** Ask the database for the full text of this enquiry, plus this particular business's own settings.

**Is it at the right stage?** An enquiry is only read once. If it has already been read, or the business hasn't finished setting up, we quietly stop instead of doing the work twice.

### The AI reads it

**Start the stopwatch.** We note the time and the size of what we're about to send, so we can report exactly how long the AI took and what it cost.

**Ask Google's AI.** We call Google directly rather than through n8n's ready-made AI step — deliberately. Only the direct call reports the **exact** number of tokens used, including the ones the AI spends thinking before it answers. Those hidden thinking tokens are why our first cost estimate was 36 times too low.

**If Google is down, OpenAI answers instead.** Same instructions, different company. A full-outage drill proved the pipeline finishes on the backup and the answer is still grounded.

**Make both answers look alike.** The two companies format replies differently. One small step rewrites either into a single shape, so nothing downstream needs to know who answered.

**Check the answer is usable.** Is the verdict one of the three we allow? Is the confidence a real number? Are the facts shaped correctly? A confident-sounding but malformed answer gets caught right here.

**Record what the call cost** — into the database, and off to the tracing dashboard, with its exact token count and price.

### One more try — then save, or ask a person

**If the first answer was unusable, we ask once more.** Same email, same instructions, a fresh attempt — with the same Google-then-OpenAI arrangement behind it, and its cost recorded just the same.

**Save the facts.** The verdict and every extracted fact are written to the enquiry's record in one go, and the enquiry moves to its next stage.

This save is **guarded**: it only applies if the enquiry is still at the stage we expect. That condition is what makes it impossible to process the same enquiry twice into a mess — the database enforces it, not the workflow.

**If the second answer was also unusable, a person takes over.** The enquiry is marked as needing review with the original email untouched. The AI having a bad day becomes someone's task, never a wrong fact in the record.

### Handing on

**Did it actually work?** Check the enquiry really did reach the "facts extracted" stage before going any further.

**Write the next job ticket** — same business, same enquiry, same tracking number, now stamped as coming from this step.

**Call the next workflow**, which works out how promising this enquiry is.

Spam and non-enquiries stop here, on purpose. They've been read, judged and recorded — there's simply nothing worth replying to.

## The rule this whole step protects

**Blank beats invented.**

The AI is told: if a fact isn't clearly in the email, leave it empty. Don't infer, don't assume, don't be helpful.

That's why a malformed answer becomes a person's job instead of a best guess — and it's why, across the whole test set, **not one fact was ever invented**.
